title: Joe Cohen on Dentons' fleetAI: 'It Gives Unique Perspectives'
pub: Artificial Lawyer (Q&A interview; Dentons UK/Ireland/Middle East Head of Innovation)
author: Joe Cohen

dom.t: Legal software: Workflow layers defend specialist value

st.t: Legal software: Workflow layers defend specialist value
st.an: Cohen’s account supports the cluster’s emphasis on governed, lawyer-facing deployment: fleetAI enables confidential GPT-4 use on client work, with guardrails and user guidance, while privacy, confidentiality and retention are treated as adoption conditions. It also provides a firm-wide uptake example, though its accuracy and safety claims are self-reported and it does not establish human verification practices or comparative performance.
qs: The platform essentially allows us to use GPT4 on our client work in a safe, confidential manner – both for chat and for document upload.

**What inspired you to do this?**  I presented to our Executive Committee in February about ChatGPT and everyone was really on board with the potential of the underlying technology and what it could mean for law firms, if the various concerns (data privacy, confidentiality, and retention) could be solved.

kp.k: Firm-wide GPT4 deployment supports chat and client-document analysis
kp.d: Joe Cohen, Dentons’ Head of Innovation for UK, Ireland and Middle East, reports that fleetAI development began in March 2023 and the platform launched firm-wide in September. He describes it as enabling confidential GPT4 use for client work through chat and document uploads, and claims throughput exceeding 7m words per minute. His satisfaction with accuracy is qualified by guardrails and guidance; the interview supplies no measured accuracy results.
qs: Yes, we have been working on fleetAI since March of this year.
The project was really condensed in terms of the timeframes, and it was amazing to be able to have launched it firm-wide in September.
The platform essentially allows us to use GPT4 on our client work in a safe, confidential manner – both for chat and for document upload.
The platform can analyse and generate over 7m words per minute and we’re really happy about levels of accuracy, pursuant to the various guardrails and (particularly) guidance we’ve put in place.

kp.k: Leadership support and technology partnerships enabled rapid deployment
kp.d: Cohen attributes the project’s head start to Executive Committee support following a February presentation, relationships with Microsoft, and development partner Springbok.AI. Leadership enthusiasm was conditional on resolving data privacy, confidentiality and retention concerns. He claims Dentons was the first law firm to launch a robust, client-safe GPT4 tool firm-wide; this is his competitive-positioning assertion rather than an independently established finding.
qs: I presented to our Executive Committee in February about ChatGPT and everyone was really on board with the potential of the underlying technology and what it could mean for law firms, if the various concerns (data privacy, confidentiality, and retention) could be solved.
We wanted to be right at the cutting edge of the legal industry on this, and as we were the first law firm to launch a robust client-safe GPT4 tool firm-wide, I think we have achieved that.

kp.k: Access extends beyond lawyers, with enthusiastic staff and clients
kp.d: Cohen reports use across the firm following the September launch, with access available to all staff rather than lawyers alone. He believes most staff had not previously used ChatGPT for work-related queries and describes firm encouragement and response quality as stimulating enthusiasm for innovation. As an indication of client interest, he reports about 7-10 AI-related client meetings per week; no adoption percentage is provided.
qs: The tool was launched in September and is already used across the firm.

I think most of our staff (the tool is available to everyone, not just lawyers) hadn’t really used ChatGPT on work-related queries before and when the firm started to actively encourage them to do so, the high quality of the responses definitely caused some shockwaves!
The client response has also been overwhelming – I’m having about 7-10 client meetings per week to discuss AI at the moment!

kp.k: Efficiency gains anticipated from contract-specific automated reports
kp.d: Cohen identifies faster, more efficient delivery as the main short-term benefit, particularly from contract-specific automated reports expected to go live toward the end of 2023. This is an anticipated operational benefit, not a quantified finding about realised time savings, costs or fees.
qs: Well, in the short term there is a lot of work that can be delivered faster and more efficiently, particularly when our contract-specific automated reports go live towards the end of this year.

kp.k: Interactive prompting offers additional perspectives on legal work
kp.d: Beyond efficiency, Cohen reports staff using creative prompts for inspiration. Examples include asking fleetAI to solicit transaction context before answering, and asking which legal questions it would raise about a document. He presents these interactions as a source of immediate, distinctive perspectives rather than as autonomous delivery of legal advice.
qs: This will be the main benefit – but what we are seeing is that people are being incredibly creative with the questions they are asking and the responses they are getting, and this extra inspiration is being noticed.

For example, asking the tool to ask you questions so you can give it necessary context to the transaction before answering your main question, or asking what legal questions it itself would ask of the document in question (this is a fun one!), can give really unique and interesting perspectives instantly.

kp.k: Expansion depends on daily adoption and practical technology understanding
kp.d: Asked about a five-year horizon, Cohen stresses uncertainty and instead proposes spending the next 12 months consolidating benefits from existing advanced LLMs, potentially with some fine tuning. He conditions expansion on majority daily usage and staff understanding of practical capabilities and limitations. His expectation of GPT5 the following year and potentially expansive subsequent opportunities is speculative.
qs: Really difficult to say. For the next 12 months, for us anyway, I think it’ll be about consolidating the benefit that you can get from the advanced LLMs as they are, maybe with a little bit of fine tuning.

Once we are in a place where the majority of our staff are using fleetAI every day as it is, we can start to look to expand – but it’s difficult to do that until everyone understands what the tech can and can’t do on a practical level.
After that, with GPT5 coming next year, the sky could really be the limit.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Joe Cohen claims fleetAI enables confidential GPT4 use on client work and predicts faster, more efficient delivery, especially through forthcoming automated contract reports.
pts.d: Cohen describes fleetAI as supporting chat and document upload in a client-safe environment. He reports capacity to analyse and generate over seven million words per minute and satisfaction with accuracy under the firm's guardrails and guidance. He identifies efficiency as the principal near-term benefit, particularly once contract-specific automated reports launch. He also claims Dentons was the first law firm to launch a robust, client-safe GPT4 tool firm-wide; this is Cohen's claim, rather than an independently established finding in the interview.

pts.k: Cohen reports that interactive prompting provides immediate additional perspectives on transactions and documents.
pts.d: Beyond efficiency, Cohen describes staff using fleetAI creatively to elicit contextual questions before a substantive answer or to suggest legal questions about a document. He presents these uses as providing inspiration and distinctive perspectives. These examples concern augmentation of staff thinking, not a claim that AI autonomously delivers legal advice or replaces lawyers.

pts.k: Cohen reports increased enthusiasm for technology among staff and substantial client interest in AI.
pts.d: He says fleetAI is already used across the firm and that actively encouraging work-related use exposed many staff to responses they found strikingly high quality. He links this experience to increased enthusiasm for innovation and reports approximately seven to ten client meetings weekly about AI. These are claims about reception and engagement, not quantified improvements in legal outcomes or evidence of universal daily adoption.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered is Cohen's firsthand implementation experience, qualitative observations and self-reported operational figures.
pts.d: As Dentons' Head of Innovation for the UK, Ireland and Middle East, Cohen draws on the platform's development and rollout, staff prompting examples, perceived response quality and client discussions. The interview supplies a throughput figure and a weekly client-meeting range, but no measurement methods, named benchmarks, accuracy rates, controlled productivity comparisons or independent validation. The contract-report efficiency benefit is prospective, while the additional-perspective claim is supported by descriptions of existing use.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Near-term gains follow the September 2023 rollout, with contract reports expected by year-end; further expansion depends on widespread daily use and practical understanding.
pts.d: In this 2023 interview, Cohen dates development to March and firm-wide launch to September. Automated contract reports are expected toward the end of 2023. Over the following twelve months, his stated priority is consolidating benefits from existing advanced LLMs, possibly with limited fine-tuning. He conditions expansion on a majority of staff using fleetAI daily and understanding its capabilities and limits. Client-work deployment is framed around resolving privacy, confidentiality and retention concerns, while accuracy is qualified by guardrails and guidance. Asked about five years ahead, he explicitly expresses uncertainty: his expectation of GPT5 'next year' and expansive possibilities is an attributed forecast, not a concrete five-year outcome.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claims primarily concern Dentons lawyers, other staff and clients, rather than profession-wide employment or market restructuring.
pts.d: Cohen describes access for all staff, not only lawyers, with potential benefits in work speed, efficiency, document and transaction analysis, and inspiration. Clients are affected through the platform's use on their matters and anticipated delivery improvements; their present interest is illustrated by AI meetings. Although Cohen discusses law-firm potential and responds to a sector-wide question, the substantive implementation claims concern Dentons. He does not predict changes in staffing numbers, billing models, ALSP market share or access to justice.
